items.title: Constant metric rescaling preserves the connection and Ricci tensor and inversely scales scalar and sectional curvature
items.statement:
Assume the inherited $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]);
the local calculations below use no further choice principle.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth manifold, let $\gamma$ be a Riemannian metric on
$\Sigma$ ([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]) and let
$\lambda>0$ be a constant. Write $\gamma_\lambda:=\lambda\gamma$ for the
rescaled metric. Then:

**(a) Connection.** The Levi-Civita connection of $\gamma_\lambda$ equals the
Levi-Civita connection of $\gamma$
([[prop-christoffel-formula-for-the-levi-civita-connection]]).

**(b) Curvature operator.** If $R_\lambda$ and $R$ are the curvature operators
of the two Levi-Civita connections in the convention
$R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$
([[prop-coordinate-formula-for-the-curvature-tensor]],
[[thm-curvature-is-a-type-one-three-tensor]]), then $R_\lambda=R$: the two
operators are equal as $(1,3)$-tensor fields.

**(c) Ricci and scalar curvature.** With the Ricci curvature of
[[def-ricci-curvature]] and the scalar curvature of [[def-scalar-curvature]],

$$\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma_\lambda)=\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma),\qquad S(\gamma_\lambda)=\lambda^{-1}S(\gamma).$$

**(d) Lowered curvature and sectional curvature.** With the Riemann four-tensor
of [[def-riemann-curvature-four-tensor]],

$$\operatorname{Rm}_{\gamma_\lambda}(X,Y,Z,W)=\lambda\,\operatorname{Rm}_\gamma(X,Y,Z,W),$$

and for every tangent two-plane $\sigma$ on which $\gamma$ is defined the
sectional curvature scales inversely,
$K_{\gamma_\lambda}(\sigma)=\lambda^{-1}K_\gamma(\sigma)$ ([[def-sectional-curvature]]).

references.title: John M. Lee, Riemannian Manifolds: An Introduction to Curvature, Chapter 3 (homotheties and the behavior of curvature under constant scaling of the metric), printed pp. 38-42, and the model-space curvatures, printed pp. 148-149
Ved Datar, Lectures on Riemannian Geometry, Lecture 8 (the Christoffel formula) and Lecture 11 (the coordinate curvature formula), printed pp. 49 and 71-72

items.title: The constant-curvature spatial model of a homogeneous cosmology
items.statement:
This item assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as inherited through the Riemannian
items cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]); no further choice principle is
used.

**(a) The datum.** Let $\Sigma$ be a connected smooth three-manifold without
boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]]) and let $\gamma$ be a Riemannian metric on
$\Sigma$ ([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]). Let
$k\in\{-1,0,1\}$. The pair $(\Sigma,\gamma)$ is a **spatial model of constant
normalized curvature $k$**, with **normalized curvature parameter** $k$, when

$$\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)=2k\,\gamma\qquad\text{at every point of }\Sigma ,$$

where $\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)$ is the Ricci curvature of $\gamma$
([[def-ricci-curvature]]). We then call $(\Sigma,\gamma,k)$ a **spatial model
datum**. The signs are named for orientation only: $k=+1$ is called the
**closed** or **positively curved** case, $k=0$ the **flat** case and $k=-1$
the **open** or **negatively curved** case; no topological content is attached
to these names by this definition.

**(b) Status of the condition.** The condition in (a) is pointwise and local.
It neither asserts nor implies that $\Sigma$ is complete, compact, simply
connected or geodesically complete, and it does not determine the global
model: this definition proves no classification theorem and this page assumes
none. In dimension three the condition is equivalent to the statement that
$\gamma$ has constant sectional curvature $k$; the companion lemma on
constant-curvature three-manifolds, recorded in the Remarks, proves that
equivalence. What is used by the cosmological deductions of this page is
exactly the Ricci form displayed in (a).

**(c) Normalization and scale.** The condition (a) fixes the numerical
curvature to $k\in\{-1,0,1\}$. For a constant $\lambda>0$, put
$\gamma'=\lambda^2\gamma$. Then

$$\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma')=\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)=2k\gamma=2(k/\lambda^2)\gamma',$$

and $K_{\gamma'}=k/\lambda^2$
([[lem-gr-constant-rescaling-preserves-levi-civita-and-curvature]]).
The sign is unchanged, but for $k\ne0$ the normalized condition (a) is
preserved only when $\lambda=1$; the flat condition is preserved for every
$\lambda>0$. Conversely, if $\operatorname{Ric}(h)=2\kappa h$ for a real
constant $\kappa\ne0$, the metric $\gamma=|\kappa|h$ satisfies
$\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)=2\operatorname{sgn}(\kappa)\gamma$ by the same
Ricci invariance, so it restores the normalization. A physical model assigns
its spatial length scale through the further factor in the model postulate.

**(d) Standard models.** For each $k\in\{-1,0,1\}$ at least one complete,
connected, boundaryless, simply connected model satisfying (a) is available:

- For $k=+1$, take the round unit sphere $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$ with its
  induced metric. Its constant curvature $+1$, completeness and connected
  boundaryless Riemannian structure are supplied by
  [[prop-round-sphere-model-geometry]] with $n=3$, $R=1$ (the curvature
  calculation is also [[ex-the-round-sphere-has-positive-constant-sectional-curvature]]);
  its simple connectedness is [[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]].
- For $k=0$, take $\mathbb R^3$ with the standard metric. Its Riemannian
  structure and vanishing curvature are [[ex-euclidean-space-has-zero-curvature]].
  It is nonempty and convex, hence simply connected by
  [[thm-convex-subsets-have-trivial-fundamental-group]], and thus connected by
  [[thm-path-connected-implies-connected]]. For completeness, the constant
  metric coefficients give zero Christoffel symbols
  ([[prop-christoffel-formula-for-the-levi-civita-connection]]); for every
  initial position $p$ and velocity $v$, the all-time curve $t\mapsto p+tv$
  solves the coordinate geodesic equation
  ([[prop-coordinate-geodesic-equation]]). Uniqueness of the maximal geodesic
  ([[thm-existence-uniqueness-and-smooth-dependence-of-geodesics]]) identifies
  it with that curve, so every maximal geodesic has domain $\mathbb R$.
  Hopf–Rinow ([[thm-hopf-rinow]]) then gives metric completeness; its
  hypotheses hold because $\mathbb R^3$ is nonempty, connected and boundaryless.
- For $k=-1$, take the upper half-space $\{x\in\mathbb R^3:x^3>0\}$ with
  $y=x^3$ and metric $y^{-2}\sum_{a=1}^3dx^a\otimes dx^a$.
  Its complete, connected, boundaryless, simply connected Riemannian
  structure and constant curvature $-1$ are exactly the $n=3$, $a=1$
  instance of [[prop-half-space-model-geometry]].

By the companion lemma recorded in the Remarks, constant sectional curvature
$k$ in dimension three gives $\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)=2k\gamma$, so each
model satisfies (a) and each sign is realized. A model datum restricts to one
of these global standard models only when its postulate says so.

items.title: Constant-curvature three-manifolds: equivalence of constant sectional curvature, the tensor identity and the Ricci condition
items.statement:
This item assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as inherited through
[[def-constant-sectional-curvature-and-space-form]]; the pointwise tensor
arguments below use no further choice principle
([[def-countable-choice]]).

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold and let $\gamma$ be a Riemannian
metric on $\Sigma$ ([[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]), with
curvature operator $R$, Riemann four-tensor $\operatorname{Rm}$
([[def-riemann-curvature-four-tensor]]), Ricci curvature
$\operatorname{Ric}$ ([[def-ricci-curvature]]) and scalar curvature $S$
([[def-scalar-curvature]]). Let $k\in\mathbb R$. The following three
statements are equivalent:

**(a)** The metric $\gamma$ has constant sectional curvature $k$: every
tangent two-plane has sectional curvature $k$
([[def-constant-sectional-curvature-and-space-form]],
[[def-sectional-curvature]]).

**(b)** $\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)=2k\gamma$ at every point of $\Sigma$; that
is the curvature condition for the real parameter $k$. When $\Sigma$ is
connected and boundaryless and $k\in\{-1,0,1\}$, it is precisely the
normalized spatial-model condition of [[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]].

**(c)** $R(X,Y)Z=k\bigl(\gamma(Y,Z)X-\gamma(X,Z)Y\bigr)$ for all smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on $\Sigma$
([[prop-curvature-tensor-of-constant-sectional-curvature]]).

Whenever these hold, the scalar curvature is $S=6k$, and the trace-free Ricci
tensor vanishes, $\operatorname{Ric}_0=0$
([[def-kulkarni-nomizu-product-trace-free-ricci-and-weyl-curvature]]).

items.title: FLRW model data: warped product metric, cosmic time, comoving congruence, scale factor and Hubble parameter
items.statement:
This item assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the tangent-bundle and
manifold-product suppliers cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]); no further
choice principle is used.

**(a) Data.** Let $c>0$ be a real constant. An **FLRW model datum with
conversion constant $c$** is a tuple

$$(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$$

consisting of:

1. a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, the **time interval**
   ([[def-interval]]);
2. a spatial model datum $(\Sigma,\gamma,k)$: a connected smooth
   three-manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary, a Riemannian metric $\gamma$ on
   $\Sigma$, and a normalized curvature parameter $k\in\{-1,0,1\}$ with
   $\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)=2k\gamma$
   ([[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]], [[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]],
   [[def-smooth-manifold]]);
3. a **scale factor**: a smooth map $a:I\to(0,\infty)$, with values in the open
   interval of strictly positive reals
   ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]).

Its **spacetime** is the product manifold $M:=I\times\Sigma$ with the product
smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]),
a smooth four-manifold without boundary. We write $t:M\to I$ for the first
coordinate function, the **cosmic time**, and $\dot a:=\frac{d}{dt}a$ for the
derivative of the scale factor ([[def-derivative]]).

**(b) The FLRW metric.** In product charts $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with $x^0=t$,
where $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ is a smooth chart of $\Sigma$, define the component functions

$$g_{00}:=-c^2,\qquad g_{0i}:=g_{i0}:=0,\qquad g_{ij}:=a(t)^2\gamma_{ij},\qquad i,j\in\{1,2,3\}.$$

These functions are smooth on the chart domain, and they define a smooth
symmetric covariant two-tensor field $g$ on $M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]): the component transformation
law is that of a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor because the definitions agree on
chart overlaps, the time component is constant and the spatial components are
multiplied by the common smooth factor $a(t)^2$. The field $g$ is the
**FLRW metric** of the datum; we write the standard informal display
$g=-c^2\,dt^2+a(t)^2\,\gamma$, meaning the symmetric tensor $-c^2\,dt\otimes dt+a(t)^2\gamma$.
That $g$ is a Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ and that the coordinate field $\partial_t$ is a time
orientation for it are not asserted by this definition but proved in
[[lem-gr-flrw-metric-and-comoving-data]] on this page; the same holds for the
clauses below that use the metric's causal classification.

**(c) Comoving congruence and cosmic time direction.** The **comoving
congruence** of the datum is the smooth vector field
$n:=c^{-1}\partial_t$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). By
[[lem-gr-flrw-metric-and-comoving-data]] the field $n$ is a smooth
future-directed unit timelike field, $g(n,n)=-1$, and the **comoving
observers** of the datum are its maximal integral curves; in product
coordinates the integral curve through $(t_0,x)$ is
$s\mapsto(t_0+s/c,x)$ on $c(I-t_0)$. Its proper-time parametrization is the
**comoving curve** $t\mapsto(t,x)$ on $I$, with constant spatial coordinate
$x\in\Sigma$ and velocity $U=cn=\partial_t$.

**(d) Hubble parameter and expansion.** The **Hubble parameter** of the datum
is the smooth function

$$H:=\frac{\dot a}{a}:I\to\mathbb R .$$

No field equation, no matter content, no equation of state, no measured value
and no claim about nature is part of this definition: an FLRW model datum is a
geometric object, and the physical reading of $c$, of $t$ as a clock reading,
of $n$ as the matter rest congruence and of $H$ as an expansion rate is
recorded in the physical postulates of the framework, not here.

items.title: The FLRW metric is smooth Lorentzian; comoving curves are unit-speed observers and cosmic time is their proper time; the slices carry the scaled spatial metric
items.statement:
Let $(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$ be an FLRW model datum with conversion constant
$c>0$, with spacetime $M=I\times\Sigma$, metric $g=-c^2dt^2+a(t)^2\gamma$ and
comoving congruence $n=c^{-1}\partial_t$
([[def-gr-flrw-model-data]], [[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]]). Then:

**(a)** The field $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
on $M$, and $N:=\partial_t$ satisfies $g(N,N)=-c^2<0$ at every point; hence
$(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

**(b)** The comoving congruence $n=c^{-1}\partial_t$ is a smooth
future-directed unit timelike vector field on $M$: $g(n,n)=-1$ and
$g(n,N)=-c<0$ at every point
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Its maximal integral
curve through $(t_0,x)$ is $\eta_{t_0,x}(s)=(t_0+s/c,x)$ on
$c(I-t_0)=\{c(t-t_0):t\in I\}$. Reparametrizing by cosmic time gives the
**comoving curve** $\gamma_x(t):=(t,x)$ on $I$; each is a future timelike
worldline whose parameter $t$ is its proper time up to an additive constant:
for $t_0,t_1\in I$ with $t_0<t_1$, the proper-time increment between
$\gamma_x(t_0)$ and $\gamma_x(t_1)$ is $t_1-t_0$
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]],
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]). The physical
four-velocity of a comoving observer is $U=\partial_t=cn$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

**(c)** The congruence $n$ is $g$-orthogonal to the spatial slices: for every
$t_0\in I$, the slice inclusion $\iota_{t_0}:\Sigma\to M$, $x\mapsto(t_0,x)$,
is a smooth embedding, the pullback $\iota_{t_0}^*g=a(t_0)^2\gamma$ is a
Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and $g(n,\iota_{t_0*}v)=0$ for every
$v\in T_x\Sigma$. Moreover the slice metric $\gamma_{t_0}:=a(t_0)^2\gamma$
has Ricci curvature $\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma_{t_0})=2k\gamma$ and constant
sectional curvature $k/a(t_0)^2$
([[lem-gr-constant-rescaling-preserves-levi-civita-and-curvature]],
[[lem-gr-constant-curvature-three-manifold-ricci]]).

items.title: Christoffel symbols of the FLRW metric in product charts
items.statement:
Let $(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$ be an FLRW model datum with conversion constant
$c>0$, with spacetime $M=I\times\Sigma$, metric $g$ and comoving congruence
$n=c^{-1}\partial_t$ ([[def-gr-flrw-model-data]]), and let $\nabla$ be the
metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Let
$(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be a product chart with $x^0=t$, where $(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ is
a smooth chart of $\Sigma$, and let ${}^{(3)}\Gamma^i{}_{jk}$ be the Christoffel symbols of
the Riemannian metric $\gamma$ in that three-dimensional chart
([[prop-christoffel-formula-for-the-levi-civita-connection]]). Write
$\dot a$ for the derivative of the scale factor and $H=\dot a/a$ for the
Hubble parameter. Then in the product chart the Christoffel symbols
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) are:

**(a)** $\Gamma^0{}_{00}=\Gamma^0{}_{0i}=\Gamma^0{}_{i0}=0$ and
$\Gamma^i{}_{00}=0$ for $i=1,2,3$;

**(b)** $\Gamma^0{}_{ij}=\Gamma^0{}_{ji}=\dfrac{a\dot a}{c^2}\,\gamma_{ij}$
for $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$;

**(c)** $\Gamma^i{}_{0j}=\Gamma^i{}_{j0}=H\,\delta^i{}_j$ for
$i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$;

**(d)** $\Gamma^i{}_{jk}={}^{(3)}\Gamma^i{}_{jk}$ for
$i,j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$.

All components not listed vanish; equivalently, the only nonzero symbols are
those in (b)-(d).

items.title: The comoving congruence is geodesic; its expansion is three Hubble parameters per unit conversion constant
items.statement:
Let $(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$ be an FLRW model datum with conversion constant
$c>0$, with spacetime $M=I\times\Sigma$, metric $g$, comoving congruence
$n=c^{-1}\partial_t$ and Hubble parameter $H=\dot a/a$
([[def-gr-flrw-model-data]], [[lem-gr-flrw-metric-and-comoving-data]]), and
let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]). Then:

**(a)** $\nabla_{\partial_t}\partial_t=0$ and $\nabla_nn=0$; consequently the
comoving curves are geodesics of $\nabla$ with affine parameter $t$, the
parameter $t$ is their proper time, and $n$ is a geodesic unit timelike
congruence in the sense of
[[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]).

**(b)** The **expansion** of the comoving congruence
$\vartheta:=\nabla_an^a$
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] clause (b),
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) is the constant-in-space
function

$$\vartheta=\frac{3H}{c}.$$

**(c)** For the physical four-velocity field $U=\partial_t=cn$ of the comoving
observers, $\nabla_aU^a=3H$, so that
$H=\tfrac13\nabla_aU^a$; the acceleration of the comoving congruence,
$a^b:=n^a\nabla_an^b$, vanishes identically
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] clause (b)).

items.title: Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors of the FLRW metric in product charts
items.statement:
Let $(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$ be an FLRW model datum with conversion constant
$c>0$, with spacetime $M=I\times\Sigma$ and metric $g$
([[def-gr-flrw-model-data]], [[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]]), let $\nabla$ be
its metric-selected connection, and let $R^a{}_{bcd}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ be the curvature components, Ricci
tensor, scalar curvature and Einstein tensor of $\nabla$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]). In a product chart
$(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ with $x^0=t$, with $\dot a$ the derivative of the scale
factor and $H=\dot a/a$:

**(a)** $\operatorname{Ric}_{00}=-\dfrac{3\ddot a}{a}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{0i}=0$, and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=\Bigl(\dfrac{a\ddot a+2\dot a^2}{c^2}+2k\Bigr)\gamma_{ij}$
for $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$;

**(b)** $S=6\Bigl(\dfrac{\ddot a}{ac^2}+\dfrac{H^2}{c^2}+\dfrac{k}{a^2}\Bigr)$;

**(c)** $G_{00}=\dfrac{3(\dot a^2+kc^2)}{a^2}$, $G_{0i}=0$, and
$G_{ij}=-\Bigl(\dfrac{2a\ddot a+\dot a^2}{c^2}+k\Bigr)\gamma_{ij}$ for
$i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$.

All displayed component functions are smooth on the chart domain; the
identities are equalities of the components of the respective tensor fields
in the product chart and hold at every point.

items.title: The Friedmann, acceleration and continuity equations of an FLRW model datum
items.statement:
**(a) Data.** A **Friedmann-system datum** is a tuple

$$(c,G_N,\Lambda,I,k,a,\varepsilon,p)$$

consisting of positive real constants $c>0$ and $G_N>0$, a real constant
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$
([[def-interval]]), a real number $k$ (the **curvature parameter** of the
datum), and smooth functions $a:I\to(0,\infty)$, $\varepsilon:I\to\mathbb R$
and $p:I\to\mathbb R$, with values in the open interval of strictly positive
reals in the case of $a$
([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). We write
$\dot a,\ddot a,\dot\varepsilon$ for the derivatives of these functions of one
variable and

$$H:=\frac{\dot a}{a}:I\to\mathbb R$$

for the **Hubble parameter** of the datum ([[def-derivative]]). No relation
between $k$ and the three signs $\{-1,0,1\}$ is imposed by this definition;
the spatial model data of [[def-gr-flrw-model-data]] restrict to those signs,
and the real parameter is used so that the equations can also be examined
after a rescaling of the spatial metric.

**(b) The equations.** For a Friedmann-system datum define the following three
scalar equations on $I$:

**(F) The Friedmann equation.**

$$H(t)^2+\frac{kc^2}{a(t)^2}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{3c^2}\,\varepsilon(t)+\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}\qquad\text{for all }t\in I;$$

**(A) The acceleration equation.**

$$\frac{\ddot a(t)}{a(t)}=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{3c^2}\bigl(\varepsilon(t)+3p(t)\bigr)+\frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}\qquad\text{for all }t\in I;$$

**(C) The continuity equation.**

$$\dot\varepsilon(t)+3H(t)\bigl(\varepsilon(t)+p(t)\bigr)=0\qquad\text{for all }t\in I .$$

We also record the **spatial-component equation**

**(S)**

$$-\frac{2a(t)\ddot a(t)+\dot a(t)^2}{c^2}-k+\Lambda a(t)^2=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,p(t)\,a(t)^2\qquad\text{for all }t\in I .$$

Each of (F), (A), (C), (S) is an equality of real numbers at each point of
$I$; the equations involve the data of clause (a) alone. Their relation to the
curvature components of an FLRW metric, and their logical relations among one
another, are the content of the results on this page and are not asserted by
this definition. In particular, this definition adopts no equation of state:
a relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$, when used, is an additional datum.

items.title: Equivalence of the Friedmann and acceleration systems, and the derivation of acceleration from Friedmann and continuity where the Hubble parameter does not vanish
items.statement:
Let $(c,G_N,\Lambda,I,k,a,\varepsilon,p)$ be a Friedmann-system datum, with the
equations (F), (A), (C), (S) as in
[[def-gr-flrw-friedmann-system]] and $H=\dot a/a$. Then:

**(a)** On the interval $I$, the pair of equations (F) and (S) holds if and
only if the pair of equations (F) and (A) holds.

**(b)** If (F) and (C) hold on $I$ and $t_0\in I$ satisfies
$H(t_0)\neq0$, then equation (A) holds at $t_0$. In particular, on any
subinterval on which $H$ has no zero, (F) and (C) imply (A).

The proof of (b) divides by $H(t_0)$; the proposition makes no claim about
points with $H(t_0)=0$, and no claim that (F) and (C) alone determine the
second derivative of $a$ there.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 8 (8.33)-(8.36): the 00 and ij equations and the elimination of second derivatives leading to the Friedmann equations, printed pp. 222-223 (PDF pp. 229-230)

items.title: Adopted homogeneous and isotropic cosmological model with a comoving perfect fluid
items.statement:
Adopt as the geometry and matter content of a **homogeneous cosmological
model** of the classical gravitational framework, to be used together with
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]],
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] and the field law of
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]], the following assumptions.

**(i) Spacetime geometry.** The model's spacetime is an FLRW model datum
$(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$ with the framework's conversion constant $c>0$, its
metric $g=-c^2dt^2+a(t)^2\gamma$ and its comoving congruence
$n=c^{-1}\partial_t$ ([[def-gr-flrw-model-data]],
[[lem-gr-flrw-metric-and-comoving-data]]). The spatial model
$(\Sigma,\gamma,k)$ is one of the standard complete simply connected models of
[[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]] clause (d), with normalized curvature parameter
$k\in\{-1,0,1\}$: the round unit three-sphere for $k=+1$, Euclidean space for
$k=0$, or hyperbolic three-space for $k=-1$; by
[[lem-gr-constant-curvature-three-manifold-ricci]] each of these carries
constant sectional curvature $k$ and $\operatorname{Ric}(\gamma)=2k\gamma$.
The name **homogeneous and isotropic cosmological model** denotes here the
explicit standard-spatial-model FLRW ansatz just specified. Its operative
geometric assumptions are the chosen global standard model, the displayed
metric and the curvature condition; the deductions do not use an additional
undefined symmetry premise. The identification of the coordinate
$t$ with the readings of ideal comoving clocks is not part of this clause: it
is the separate clock rule of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]], applied
only where a physical clock reading is asserted. The
mathematical content used by the deductions of this page is the FLRW form
displayed above together with the curvature condition; no classification
theorem, and no transitivity statement about isometry groups, is proved or
used here.

**(ii) Matter content.** Exactly one of the following two sectors is adopted.

- **Vacuum sector.** No matter is present: the model's stress-energy tensor is
  the zero tensor, $\varepsilon=p=0$.
- **Comoving perfect-fluid sector.** The model's matter is a perfect-fluid
  model $(\varepsilon,p,n_F)$ on the matter domain $U:=M$, the model's whole
  spacetime, in the sense of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]: that is,
  $U=M$ is the nonempty open domain, $\varepsilon$ and $p$ are the smooth
  rest energy density and pressure on it, and the fluid's unit timelike
  four-velocity field $n_F$ is assumed to be the comoving congruence
  $n=c^{-1}\partial_t$ of clause (i). The density and pressure are assumed
  **homogeneous**, that is, functions of cosmic time alone:
  $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(t)$ and $p=p(t)$ in the product charts, with
  values in the units of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. The
  model additionally adopts an **explicit equation of state**, one of:
  a barotropic relation $p=P(\varepsilon)$ with $P$ a smooth real function
  defined on an open interval containing the range of $\varepsilon$; or the
  constant-parameter relation $p=w\varepsilon$ with a real constant $w$ and
  the stated domain of positive $\varepsilon$. The equation of state is an
  adopted constitutive restriction, not a consequence of the field law.
  The fluid stress-energy $T_{ab}=(\varepsilon+p)n_an_b+pg_{ab}$ is the
  gravitating source in $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=(8\pi G_N/c^4)T_{ab}$
  ([[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]). The scale factor and fluid data must
  jointly satisfy that law when a solution is claimed; the fluid is not
  treated as test matter on a separately prescribed background.

**(iii) Status, scope and exclusions.** Clauses (i) and (ii) are adopted
assumptions of the model. They are not derived from the field law, from
mathematical symmetry, or from observation; the symmetry of the ansatz
motivates but does not prove them, and no claim is made that any actual
cosmological system is exactly homogeneous, isotropic, comoving or
barotropic. The model contains no observed value: the scale factor, the
densities, the parameters $k,\Lambda,w$ and the spacetime interval are model
data, and every conclusion conditional on the model inherits the idealizations
listed in the physical scope of this item. Anisotropic stresses, heat flow and
dissipation, spatial inhomogeneities and perturbations, distributional or
lower-dimensional sources, non-smooth fields and quantum effects lie outside
the model and require additional content. Comparisons of the model's
predictions with reported observations test the combined model — geometry,
matter content, field law and the observation and analysis assumptions — and
agreement is evidence about that combination, not a proof of this postulate.

D. Tong, Cosmology (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, 2019 revision), section 1.1 and section 1.2.2: the cosmological principle, the Robertson-Walker metric (1.12) and the perfect-fluid energy-momentum tensor with equation of state P = w rho (1.35)-(1.41), printed pp. 5-11 and 26-29 (PDF pp. 11-17 and 32-35)

items.physical_scope: Adoption of the homogeneous and isotropic cosmological model of the classical gravitational framework: a spatially standard constant-curvature model, an FLRW metric with a smooth scale factor, and either the vacuum sector or a comoving perfect fluid whose density and pressure depend on cosmic time alone, with an explicit equation of state. The geometry and the matter content are adopted model assumptions, not derived results, and no observed value, redshift, distance, age, temperature or comparison with data is asserted. The model excludes anisotropic stresses, dissipation and heat flow, spatial inhomogeneities and perturbations, distributional or lower-dimensional sources, non-smooth fields, additional matter sectors or corrections to the declared perfect-fluid stress-energy, and quantum effects; the deductions conditional on the model hold only within these restrictions.

items.title: Reduction of the field equations of the homogeneous cosmological model to the Friedmann and acceleration equations, with derived continuity
items.statement:
Adopt the homogeneous cosmological model of
[[post-gr-flrw-homogeneous-cosmological-model]] with an FLRW model datum
$(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$, conversion constant $c>0$, a vacuum or comoving
perfect-fluid matter sector, and the field law of
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] with the same $c$, the parameter
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and the framework's $G_N>0$
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]],
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]]). Write
$g$ for the FLRW metric, $G_{ab}$ for its Einstein tensor, $T_{ab}$ for the
model's stress-energy tensor and, in the matter sector, let
$\varepsilon(t),p(t)$ be the homogeneous density and pressure and
$n=c^{-1}\partial_t$ the comoving congruence. Then:

**(a)** On the spacetime, the field equation
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\dfrac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}T_{ab}$ holds if and only if the
Friedmann equation (F) and the acceleration equation (A) of
[[def-gr-flrw-friedmann-system]] hold for the data
$(c,G_N,\Lambda,I,k,a,\varepsilon,p)$. Here the vacuum sector is the case
$\varepsilon=p=0$, in which $T_{ab}=0$.

**(b)** If the field equation holds, then the continuity equation (C) of
[[def-gr-flrw-friedmann-system]] holds; in the vacuum sector it holds
trivially.

No converse of (b) is asserted: the continuity equation is not claimed to
suffice for the field equation, and no existence or uniqueness of solutions of
the reduced system is asserted for any data or equation of state.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 8 (8.18)-(8.23) and (8.32)-(8.36): the perfect-fluid tensor T^mu_nu = diag(-rho, p, p, p), its 0-component conservation and the 00/ij Einstein equations reducing to the Friedmann equations, printed pp. 221-223 (PDF pp. 228-230)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), sections 4.6.1-4.6.2: the FRW Ricci and Einstein tensors, the continuity equation, the Friedmann equation (4.66) and the acceleration equation (4.67), printed pp. 200-203 (PDF pp. 207-210)

H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), section 6.4 'Einstein's equation': the field equation (6.32) and the addition of the cosmological term (6.34), printed pp. 67-68 (PDF pp. 68-69)

items.physical_scope: Conditional reduction of the adopted field law for the homogeneous and isotropic cosmological model: the field equations hold exactly when the Friedmann and acceleration equations hold for the model data, and then the continuity equation holds as a consequence of the field law. The result is conditional on the adopted geometry, matter content and field law; it asserts no measured value, no existence of solutions for arbitrary equations of state and no claim that the model describes nature.

items.title: The flat barotropic power-law solutions of the homogeneous cosmological field equations
items.statement:
Adopt the homogeneous cosmological model of
[[post-gr-flrw-homogeneous-cosmological-model]] with the flat standard spatial
model ($k=0$, Euclidean space), the field law of the model with
$\Lambda=0$, conversion constant $c>0$ and the framework's $G_N>0$, and a
comoving perfect-fluid matter sector whose equation of state is
$p=w\varepsilon$ for a real constant $w>-1$
([[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]] clause (d),
[[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]).

**(a)** Let $t_0\in\mathbb R$, let $t_*>0$ be a reference time, let $A>0$ be a
reference length, and put

$$q:=\frac{2}{3(1+w)},\qquad I:=(t_0,\infty),\qquad a(t):=A\left(\frac{t-t_0}{t_*}\right)^{q},\qquad \varepsilon(t):=\frac{3c^2q^2}{8\pi G_N\,(t-t_0)^2},$$

with $p(t):=w\varepsilon(t)$. Then the data
$(c,G_N,0,I,0,a,\varepsilon,p)$ satisfy the Friedmann equation (F) and the
acceleration equation (A) on $I$
([[def-gr-flrw-friedmann-system]]), so by
[[pthm-gr-flrw-field-equations-reduction]] the adopted field equations hold on
the spacetime $I\times\Sigma$. In particular:

- for $w=0$ (dust) one has $q=\tfrac23$ and
  $a(t)=A\bigl((t-t_0)/t_*\bigr)^{2/3}$;
- for $w=\tfrac13$ (radiation) one has $q=\tfrac12$ and
  $a(t)=A\bigl((t-t_0)/t_*\bigr)^{1/2}$.

**(b)** On $I$ the density scales as
$\varepsilon(t)=C\,a(t)^{-3(1+w)}$ with the positive constant
$C=A^{3(1+w)}\dfrac{3c^2q^2}{8\pi G_Nt_*^2}$, and the continuity
equation (C) holds.

The theorem asserts no uniqueness of solutions of the reduced system for the
stated equation of state, no extension of the solutions beyond the displayed
interval, and no value of $A,t_*,t_0$ or of the constants.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 8 (8.21)-(8.23) and (8.49): the equation of state p = w rho, rho proportional to a^{-3(1+w)} and the flat dust solution a proportional to t^{2/3}, printed pp. 221-222 and 226 (PDF pp. 228-229 and 233); (8.53): the flat radiation solution a proportional to t^{1/2}, printed p. 227 (PDF p. 234)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.6.2: the flat single-fluid power-law solutions a(t) = (t/t_0)^{2/(3+3w)} and the dust and radiation exponents, printed p. 203 (PDF p. 210)

D. Tong, Cosmology (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, 2019 revision), sections 1.2.2, 1.2.3 and 1.3.1: the density scaling rho proportional to a^{-3(1+w)} and the Einstein-de Sitter universe, printed pp. 28-29 and 33-34 (PDF pp. 34-35 and 39-40)

items.physical_scope: Explicit exact solutions of the adopted field law for the flat (k=0), Lambda=0 homogeneous model with a comoving perfect fluid whose equation of state is p = w epsilon with a constant w > -1, on a open half-line: the expanding power-law scale factors and their energy densities. The statement is a conditional verification inside the adopted model; it asserts no uniqueness, no extension beyond the displayed interval, no value of the constants, and no comparison with observations.

items.title: The flat vacuum solutions with a cosmological parameter: exponential expansion for Lambda positive and non-existence for Lambda negative
items.statement:
Adopt the homogeneous cosmological model of
[[post-gr-flrw-homogeneous-cosmological-model]] with the flat standard spatial
model ($k=0$, Euclidean space), the field law with the framework's constants
$c>0$, $G_N>0$ and a cosmological parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and the
vacuum matter sector, so that $T_{ab}=0$ and $\varepsilon=p=0$
([[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]] clause (d),
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]). Then:

**(a)** If $\Lambda>0$, then for every $t_0\in\mathbb R$ and every $A>0$ the
datum with $I:=\mathbb R$,

$$H_\Lambda:=c\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda}{3}},\qquad a(t):=A\exp\bigl(H_\Lambda(t-t_0)\bigr),\qquad \varepsilon(t):=0,\qquad p(t):=0$$

satisfies the Friedmann equation (F) and the acceleration equation (A) on
$\mathbb R$ ([[def-gr-flrw-friedmann-system]]), so by
[[pthm-gr-flrw-field-equations-reduction]] the field equations hold on the
spacetime $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$ with the metric
$g=-c^2dt^2+a(t)^2\gamma$.

**(b)** If $\Lambda<0$, then there is no nonempty open interval $I$ and no
smooth function $a:I\to(0,\infty)$ such that the datum
$(c,G_N,\Lambda,I,0,a,0,0)$ satisfies the Friedmann equation (F); consequently
the flat vacuum model has no solution of the field equations for $\Lambda<0$.

No uniqueness of the solutions of (a) is asserted, no numerical value of
$\Lambda,H_\Lambda,A$ or $t_0$ is asserted, and nothing is claimed about the
limit $t\to-\infty$, about singularities or about global structure.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 8 (8.58): a flat vacuum-dominated universe must have Lambda > 0 and a is proportional to exp(+/- sqrt(Lambda/3) t), printed p. 227 (PDF p. 234); (8.29)-(8.31): the vacuum energy-momentum tensor as a perfect fluid with rho = -p = Lambda/(8 pi G), printed p. 222 (PDF p. 229)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.5.2 and section 4.6.2: the cosmological-constant term in the field equation and the flat single-fluid solutions, printed pp. 182-183 and 201-203 (PDF pp. 189-190 and 208-210)
D. Tong, Cosmology (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, 2019 revision), section 1.3.3: the de Sitter universe as the vacuum-dominated solution, printed pp. 40-43 (PDF pp. 46-49)

items.physical_scope: Exact vacuum solutions of the adopted field law for the flat (k=0) homogeneous model: the exponentially expanding solution for a positive cosmological parameter, and the non-existence of any flat vacuum solution for a negative cosmological parameter. The claims are conditional on the adopted model, field law and parameter sign; no numerical value of Lambda or of the expansion rate, no assertion about singularities, global structure or observations, and no claim that the model describes nature is made.

items.title: Cosmological redshift: the observer-energy ratio of a null geodesic between comoving observers is the inverse scale-factor ratio
items.statement:
Adopt the homogeneous cosmological model of
[[post-gr-flrw-homogeneous-cosmological-model]] with an FLRW model datum
$(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$ and metric $g=-c^2dt^2+a(t)^2\gamma$
([[def-gr-flrw-model-data]]), let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), and adopt the light-ray rule that
ideal light rays are future null geodesics of $\nabla$
([[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] clause (iii)). Let
$\eta:J\to M$, $s\mapsto\eta(s)$, be such a ray: a $C^2$ curve on an interval
$J$ with tangent $V:=\eta'$, $g(V,V)=0$, $V$ future-directed, and
$\nabla_VV=0$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Let $s_E,s_R\in J$ with
$s_E<s_R$, let $t_E:=t(\eta(s_E))$ and $t_R:=t(\eta(s_R))$ be the cosmic times
of the two events, and for each $s\in J$ define the **observer energy** of the
ray at $\eta(s)$ relative to the comoving observer by

$$E(s):=-c\,g_{\eta(s)}\bigl(V(s),n(\eta(s))\bigr),\qquad n=c^{-1}\partial_t .$$

the value $E_n(V)$ of the observer-energy definition for the unit observer
$n$ ([[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]] clause (a)). Then:

**(a)** $a\bigl(t(\eta(s))\bigr)V^t(s)$ is constant along $J$, where
$V^t=dt(V)$; in particular
$a(t_R)V^t(s_R)=a(t_E)V^t(s_E)$.

**(b)** $E(s)>0$ along the ray and

$$\frac{E(s_R)}{E(s_E)}=\frac{a(t_E)}{a(t_R)} .$$

**(c)** If the **redshift parameter** of the pair of events is defined by
$z:=\dfrac{E(s_E)}{E(s_R)}-1$, that is, by $1+z=E(s_E)/E(s_R)$, then

$$1+z=\frac{a(t_R)}{a(t_E)} .$$

The ratio in (b) and (c) is unchanged if $V$ is replaced by $\mu V$ with a
positive constant $\mu>0$: a future null ray determines its tangent only up to positive scale,
and only the ratio of energies is asserted. No observed wavelength, spectral
line, distance, velocity or measurement enters the statement.

references.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 8 (8.61)-(8.67): the Killing-tensor constant of null geodesics, omega_0/omega_1 = a_1/a_0 and the redshift definition z = a_0/a_1 - 1, printed pp. 228-229 (PDF pp. 235-236)

D. Tong, Cosmology (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, 2019 revision), section 1.1.3: null paths in the Robertson-Walker metric and the redshift parameter (1.18)-(1.21), printed pp. 14-15 (PDF pp. 20-21)
D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 4.6.2: the geodesic motion of light in the FRW metric, printed pp. 203-204 (PDF pp. 210-211)

items.physical_scope: Conditional prediction of the adopted homogeneous cosmological model: the ratio of the observer energies of a specified future null geodesic measured by comoving observers at two events is the inverse ratio of the scale factor at those cosmic times, and the redshift parameter so defined satisfies 1+z = a(t_R)/a(t_E). The statement is an exact consequence of the model metric, the null-geodesic light-ray rule and the observer-energy definition; it asserts no observed redshift, no spectral line, no distant-velocity interpretation and no measurement, and it excludes non-geometric-optics propagation, dispersion and any apparatus or analysis model.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the homogeneous cosmological model: model predictions, reported observations and statistical inference are distinct
items.statement:
This note records what the items of this page do and do not establish, and how
a comparison with reported observations would have to be made. It proves
nothing and reports no measurement.

- **Everything on the page is conditional on the adopted model.** The
  geometry, the matter sector and the equation of state are adopted in
  [[post-gr-flrw-homogeneous-cosmological-model]]; the field law is adopted in
  the framework. The reduction [[pthm-gr-flrw-field-equations-reduction]]
  identifies the field equations of that model with the Friedmann and
  acceleration equations, and the solution theorems
  [[pthm-gr-flrw-power-law-solutions]] and
  [[pthm-gr-flrw-de-sitter-solutions]] verify particular data against those
  equations. The redshift relation [[pthm-gr-flrw-cosmological-redshift]] is a
  consequence of the model metric and the light-ray rule alone. No item on
  this page asserts that the universe is homogeneous, isotropic, flat, dust-
  or radiation-dominated, vacuum-dominated or described by any particular
  value of the parameters.

- **Model predictions and observations are different objects.** The items on
  this page produce model quantities: a scale factor $a(t)$, a Hubble
  parameter $H=\dot a/a$, densities $\varepsilon,p$, a curvature parameter $k$,
  a cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ and energy ratios along ideal null
  geodesics [[def-gr-flrw-model-data]], [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]].
  A reported observation, by contrast, is an apparatus- and
  calibration-dependent record: for example an identified spectral feature
  with a measured wavelength ratio, or a set of source fluxes, each with
  selection effects, resolution and uncertainty. No such record is cited,
  created or simulated on this page, and no numerical value of $H$, of a
  density, of a redshift, of a distance or of an age is asserted anywhere in
  the batch.

- **Comparison is a separate statistical inference.** To compare the model
  with data one must specify the preparation and selection of the sample, the
  measurement and calibration model of the apparatus, the relation between the
  recorded quantity and the model quantity (for instance a distance measure
  defined from fluxes and luminosities, or a temperature pattern), the
  statistical model of the sampling and the error budget, and the space of
  competing models. Each of these is an additional assumption, and the
  comparison tests the model together with them; agreement is evidence about
  the combination, and a discrepancy may equally indicate an incorrect
  auxiliary assumption, an apparatus effect or an analysis error
  (see the model's own exclusions in
  [[post-gr-flrw-homogeneous-cosmological-model]] clause (iii)). Statistical
  significance, a confidence interval and a posterior probability are
  properties of the inference, not of the theory, and a p-value is not the
  probability that a model is false.

- **Idealizations the model does not capture.** The adopted model has no
  spatial inhomogeneity or anisotropy, no anisotropic stress, no heat flow or
  dissipation, no structure formation and no quantum or non-smooth effects
  ([[post-gr-flrw-homogeneous-cosmological-model]] clause (iii),
  [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). The comoving congruence is a
  specific idealization of the matter motion, and the equation of state is an
  adopted constitutive relation with a stated domain. The spatial model is
  fixed globally among the standard constant-curvature models
  ([[def-gr-flrw-spatial-model]] clause (d)); this is model data, not a
  consequence of the local curvature condition, and no classification theorem
  is used.

- **What would be needed for an observation item.** A future experiment item
  for this page would have to retrieve and read primary sources, record the
  apparatus, preparation, calibration and sampling model, give operational
  definitions of the measured quantities, report the observations with their
  uncertainties and limitations, and separate the reported statistical
  inference from the model prediction, exactly as required for experiment
  items of the framework. Until such items exist, every statement on this
  page remains a conditional model result, and the cosmological
  interpretation of any observed redshift, distance or temperature pattern is
  a modelling and inference question, not a consequence of the mathematics
  proved here.

items.title: Direct check of the flat power-law data against the Friedmann-system equations
items.statement:
Fix real constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $A>0$, $t_*>0$, $t_0\in\mathbb R$ and
$w>-1$, and put

$$q:=\frac{2}{3(1+w)},\qquad I:=(t_0,\infty),\qquad a(t):=A\Bigl(\frac{t-t_0}{t_*}\Bigr)^{q},\qquad \varepsilon(t):=\frac{3c^2q^2}{8\pi G_N\,(t-t_0)^2},\qquad p(t):=w\,\varepsilon(t),$$

with real powers in the sense of [[def-real-power]]. Then:

1. The functions $a,\varepsilon,p$ are smooth on $I$, $a(t)>0$ and
   $\varepsilon(t)>0$ for every $t\in I$, and on $I$

$$H(t)=\frac{q}{t-t_0},\qquad \frac{\ddot a(t)}{a(t)}=\frac{q(q-1)}{(t-t_0)^2}.$$

2. The Friedmann-system datum $(c,G_N,0,I,0,a,\varepsilon,p)$ satisfies the
   Friedmann equation (F), the acceleration equation (A), the continuity
   equation (C) and the spatial-component equation (S) of
   [[def-gr-flrw-friedmann-system]] on $I$. In particular $w=0$ gives
   $q=\tfrac23$ and $w=\tfrac13$ gives $q=\tfrac12$.

items.title: Direct check of the flat vacuum data with a cosmological parameter against the Friedmann-system equations
items.statement:
Fix real constants $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $A>0$, $t_0\in\mathbb R$ and
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Then:

1. If $\Lambda>0$, put $H_\Lambda:=c\sqrt{\Lambda/3}$ and define
   $a:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ by
   $a(t):=A\exp\bigl(H_\Lambda(t-t_0)\bigr)$, together with
   $\varepsilon:=0$ and $p:=0$ on $I:=\mathbb R$. Then the Friedmann-system
   datum $(c,G_N,\Lambda,I,0,a,\varepsilon,p)$ satisfies (F), (A), (C) and
   (S) of [[def-gr-flrw-friedmann-system]] on all of $I$.
2. If $\Lambda<0$, then for every nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$
   and every smooth $a:I\to(0,\infty)$ the datum
   $(c,G_N,\Lambda,I,0,a,0,0)$ fails the Friedmann equation (F) at every point
   of $I$; in particular no such flat vacuum datum satisfies the
   Friedmann-system equations.

with $k=0$, $\Lambda=0$, constant scale factor $a\equiv A$ for some $A>0$,
constant density $\varepsilon\equiv\varepsilon_0$ for some $\varepsilon_0>0$
and pressure $p\equiv0$ satisfies the Friedmann equation (F)."

items.title: An explicit null geodesic in an exponentially expanding flat FLRW datum: constant aV^t and the observer-energy ratio
items.statement:
Fix real constants $c>0$, $A>0$, $H>0$, $t_0\in\mathbb R$, $r_0\in\mathbb R$.
Let $(I,\Sigma,\gamma,k,a)$ be the FLRW model datum with $I=\mathbb R$,
$\Sigma=\mathbb R^3$ carrying the standard Euclidean metric $\gamma$ in the
standard coordinates $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$, $k=0$ and
$a(t):=A\exp\bigl(H(t-t_0)\bigr)$
([[def-gr-flrw-model-data]], [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). On the
spacetime $M=I\times\Sigma$ define the curve $\eta:(0,\infty)\to M$,

$$\eta(s):=\Bigl(t(s),\ \Bigl(r_0+\frac{c}{AH^2s},\,0,\,0\Bigr)\Bigr),\qquad t(s):=t_0+\frac1H\log(Hs),$$

and let $V:=\eta'$ with components $V^t=dt/ds$, $V^1,V^2,V^3$. Then:

1. The curve $\eta$ is smooth and its tangent $V$ is a future-directed null
   vector, $g(V,V)=0$ and $V^t>0$, at every point of $(0,\infty)$; moreover
   $\eta$ is a geodesic of the metric-selected connection with affine
   parameter $s$, in the sense of [[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]].
2. Along $\eta$ the product $a\bigl(t(s)\bigr)V^t(s)$ is the constant $A$; in
   particular $aV^t$ is preserved by the flow of the null geodesic.
3. For $0<s_E<s_R$ let $t_E=t(s_E)$, $t_R=t(s_R)$, let $n=c^{-1}\partial_t$
   be the comoving congruence of the datum and let
   $E(s):=-c\,g_{\eta(s)}\bigl(V(s),n(\eta(s))\bigr)$ be the observer energy of
   [[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]] clause (a). Then
   $E(s)=c^2/(Hs)>0$ and

$$\frac{E(s_R)}{E(s_E)}=\frac{a(t_E)}{a(t_R)}=\frac{s_E}{s_R}.$$
